task.title: Box sizes
task.shortdesc: By default a box is as wide as the box that contains it and as high as its content. Use the size properties to give a box another size, or to limit its size.

step.cmd: Set the width and the height

info.p: The width and height properties set the preferred size of a box. Their initial value is auto, which lets layout choose the size. A size can be a length, such as 200pt, or a percentage of the size of the containing block.
The properties inline-size and block-size do the same by the direction of the text: the inline size is the width and the block size is the height in horizontal text.
The box-sizing property tells what a width or a height measures:

ul.li: content-box is the initial value. The size is the size of the content. The padding and the border are added outside it.
border-box makes the size include the padding and the border, so the content is smaller.

info.p: This note is 200pt wide from the outside of one border to the outside of the other. With content-box, it would be 228pt wide.

image.alt: Two boxes with the same width of 200pt. With content-box the content is 200pt wide and the padding and border add to 228pt. With border-box the whole box is 200pt wide and the content is 172pt.

step.cmd: Size a box from its content

info.p: These keywords can replace a length in any size property:

ul.li: min-content is the smallest size that the content can have without overflowing. For text, it is the width of the longest word.
max-content is the size that the content has when nothing wraps.
fit-content is the available space, but not less than min-content and not more than max-content. fit-content(limit) uses a length or a percentage as the available space.
stretch makes the margin box fill the available space.
contain fills the available space and keeps the aspect ratio of the box, if it has one.
calc-size() calculates a size from another size. calc-size(auto, size / 2) is half of the size that auto gives.

info.p: Minimum and maximum sizes limit the preferred size. min-width, min-height, min-inline-size and min-block-size take the same values as width. Their initial value is auto. max-width, max-height, max-inline-size and max-block-size take the same values, and none too, which is their initial value. When a minimum is larger than a maximum, the minimum wins.
This illustration fills the line, but is never wider than 40em.

The size property sets the width and the height. min-size and max-size set the two minimum sizes and the two maximum sizes. They take one or two values, and one value applies to both. With two values, the width comes first.

The aspect-ratio property gives a box a ratio between its width and its height. When you set one of the two sizes, CSSMedia calculates the other. Write the ratio as two numbers separated by a slash, such as 16 / 9, or as one number. A single number is a ratio to 1. The initial value is auto, which uses the ratio of an image if the box has one.
This frame is 320pt wide and 180pt high.

step.cmd: Give a size to a box that ignores its content

info.p: A box with contain: size is sized as if it were empty. Use contain-intrinsic-width, contain-intrinsic-height, contain-intrinsic-inline-size, contain-intrinsic-block-size, or contain-intrinsic-size for both, to give it the size that it should have instead. They take a length, or none, which is the initial value.
